text:
Tell me in about 200 words why people in India are switching to UPI, with a short list of 3 reasons
6:12 AM

People in India are switching to UPI because it makes paying someone as easy as sending a message. You open any bank or payment app, scan a code or type a phone number, enter your PIN, and the money moves in seconds. There are no cards to carry, no cash to count and no change to hunt for.

It also works almost everywhere. Chai stalls, vegetable sellers, auto drivers and big stores all show the same kind of QR code, so you pay the same way whether it's ₹20 or ₹20,000. Shopkeepers like it too, since the money lands straight in their bank account and they don't need a costly card machine.

Another big push is that it's free for most everyday payments. Because banks and apps all work together, you aren't locked into one app, and you can switch whenever you like. Add easy sign-up with just a bank account and a mobile number, plus cashback offers in the early days, and many people tried it once and never went back. Today, even small towns and villages use it daily, which has made cash feel slow by comparison.

Three main reasons:

Fast and simple: pay in seconds with a QR code or phone number.
Free and accepted everywhere: from street vendors to large shops, with no card machine needed.
Works across banks and apps: one bank account, your choice of app.

6:14 AM

Plan a 3 day trip to Jaipur for my parents
6:15 AM

Here's a relaxed 3-day Jaipur plan with a slow pace, early starts and a rest after lunch each day.

Day 1: Forts and palaces

Morning: Amer Fort. Take the jeep up so the steep climb doesn't tire them, and stop at Jal Mahal for photos on the way.
Afternoon: City Palace and Jantar Mantar after a long lunch break.
Evening: Hawa Mahal glows at sunset. A rooftop café across the road gives the best view without any walking.

Day 2: Temples, markets and culture

Morning: Govind Dev Ji Temple, then Birla Mandir.
Afternoon: Albert Hall Museum, then Johari Bazaar for jewellery and Bapu Bazaar for juttis and textiles.
Evening: Dinner and a folk show at Chokhi Dhani.

Day 3: Easy sights and a calm finish

Morning: Panna Meena ka Kund, Patrika Gate and the Anokhi Museum of Hand Printing.
Afternoon: Lunch, last-minute shopping, then leave.
Optional: Nahargarh Fort at sunset if they feel up for it.

Late October and November are pleasantly cool for Jaipur, so mornings are the best time for forts. When are they travelling, and do they need a lot of seating or lift access?
